draft.title: Porter's generic strategies
card: Michael Porter said a business gains a competitive advantage by following one of two main strategies. A competitive advantage is something that helps a business win more customers than its rivals.
the business aims to have lower costs than its rivals, so it can charge lower prices or earn a higher profit at the same price. It looks for savings, such as buying in bulk or cutting waste.
the business offers something different that customers value, such as higher quality, unique design or better service. Customers may pay a higher price for it.
In both cases the business is trying to stand out from rivals. One does it through low cost. The other does it through being different in a way customers want.
draft.remember: Cost leadership wins by lower cost. Differentiation wins by being different in a way customers value.

a.q: Which action best shows a business using a differentiation strategy?
opts: Offering a unique product with features customers value
Cutting its costs by buying supplies in large amounts
Lowering its prices to match the cheapest rival
Reducing waste so each unit costs less to make
a.why: Differentiation means being different in a way customers value, and a unique product with valued features does this. Buying in bulk and cutting waste lower costs, which is cost leadership. Matching a rival's low price is about price, not being different.
a.clue: Which option makes the product stand out, not cost less?

b.q: Tariq runs a bakery in Geelong. He buys flour in bulk, uses one simple recipe range and keeps staff numbers low, so his loaves cost less to make than rivals' loaves. Which strategy is he following, and why?
opts: Cost leadership, because he keeps his costs below rivals
Cost leadership, because he sells bread, a basic product
Differentiation, because he uses a simple recipe range
Differentiation, because he buys flour in large amounts
b.why: Tariq's actions all lower his cost per loaf, so he is following cost leadership. Having a simple recipe range does not make his bread different in a way customers value. It is a way to cut costs, so the differentiation options are wrong.
b.clue: Look at what each action does to the cost of making a loaf.

a.best: Offering a unique product with features customers value

b.best: Cost leadership, because he keeps his costs below rivals

problems.detail: The card defines competitive advantage only as winning more customers than rivals. That is too narrow: an advantage can also mean higher margins or profit. The card's own cost leadership line, 'earn a higher profit at the same price', does not fit this definition.

check.summary: Both questions have one clear right answer, and the explanations match the card. The card's definition of competitive advantage is too narrow: it leaves out higher profit or margins, which the card itself describes under cost leadership.
